//: Phase 4 positive controls. Each fault is a source patch under which one representation proof is trusted without evidence, so that a directed mutant which passes it must be caught by the differential or by --maglev-assert-types. `dgf.py canary --fault ID` applies, builds, installs and reverts.

faults.summary: BuildCheckSmi records kSmi and then elides the runtime check that would justify it, for every input.
faults.expects: any input that reaches a BuildCheckSmi site diverges in the maglev config, value-equal or not; `value-equal-check` narrows the same elision to inputs whose value is an integer Smi

faults.summary: BuildCheckSmi elides when CheckFloat64SameValue(node, IntegerSmi) holds, even if node is a HeapNumber.
faults.mutator: smi-to-heapnumber (`7` -> `7.0`, value equal, representation not) is the mutation aimed at this fault and at the `value-equal-smi` target specifically: it moves exactly the fact this proof reads, from Smi to HeapNumber, without moving any value the seed's self-check compares. C1.1 (500880819, 489280531) is this shape.
faults.expects: a store of a value-equal HeapNumber into a Smi-typed field diverges in the maglev config: `seeds/14_value_equal_smi.js` and the `-0.0` slot of the template read the field back as +0 after the store (differential, field reads `Infinity` instead of `-Infinity`). The store has to be observed through the field: Maglev forwards the stored node to a load of the same field in the same function, so the store's return value hides it. A value-equal HeapNumber that keeps its value (5.0, 0.0, a HeapNumber holding an integer) does not diverge, and 7 / 1e3 never reach the fault because they are already Smis. Clean builds do not diverge on this seed, so verdicts are canary-only.

faults.summary: Inside MaglevInliner::RunOptimizer every Smi untag is unchecked: the callee's call-feedback proof is applied to the caller's node without re-validation.
faults.expects: a caller warmed to Smi whose callee (SignedSmall feedback) is inlined, then called with a HeapNumber, aborts in UnsafeSmiUntag (Operand is not a smi) while the baseline returns normally; the gate is the inliner's optimizer run itself, so a graph that does not inline keeps the stock behavior and every Smi untag in a graph that does inline is affected

faults.summary: Untagged numeric Phi loses HeapObjectness; its CheckHeapObject is replaced by Identity.
faults.expects: any input that reaches a Phi with mixed Smi/HeapNumber input and a HeapObject consumer diverges in the maglev config

faults.summary: The back edge type is never merged into post_loop_type; the header type is promoted without re-validation.
faults.expects: any loop whose back edge merges a HeapNumber over a Smi header diverges (crash: Operand is not a smi); a peeled iteration widens the header type at build time and hides the fault, so sweep with --no-maglev-loop-peeling
